questions.text: What is the main failure risk when answering long-video questions by retrieving only selected clips?

options.A: Every retrieved clip must contain the entire original video.
options.B: Retrieval guarantees all relevant events reach the answer model.
options.C: The retriever may miss relevant evidence before the answer model sees it.
options.D: The model must generate every video frame before reading the question.

questions.explanation: Retrieval reduces context cost by selecting clips, but omitted evidence cannot inform the downstream answer. Retrieval recall becomes a key bottleneck.

questions.text: A 30-minute video is sampled at 1 FPS with 81 visual tokens per frame. Ignoring text overhead, how many visual tokens does it require?
questions.explanation: 30×60=1800 seconds; at one frame per second, 1800×81=145800 visual tokens.

questions.text: nih_trial samples a marker position and returns recall_prob from a supplied lookup curve, without calling a model. What does its output establish?

options.A: A measured model accuracy on a real long-video recall benchmark.
options.B: An observed success or failure on recognizing the inserted visual marker.
options.C: A guarantee that the downstream retriever finds the marker clip.
options.D: A simulated probability selected from the supplied curve, not measured recall.

questions.explanation: The helper chooses a probability using input assumptions. It neither invokes a video model nor tests marker recognition, so its probability is simulated.
